questions.subunit: Vertical, Corresponding, and Alternate Angles
questions.question: Two lines intersect. When one of the angles formed is 65°, what is the measure of its vertical angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal, so it is 65°.

questions.subunit: Vertical, Corresponding, and Alternate Angles
questions.question: Two lines intersect at a point. When one of the angles formed is 110°, what is the measure of the angle next to it, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180°-110°=70°.

questions.subunit: Vertical, Corresponding, and Alternate Angles
questions.question: When a line crosses two lines, what do we call the angles that lie on the same side of the crossing line and in corresponding positions?
questions.explanation: Angles in corresponding positions are corresponding angles. Angles in diagonally opposite positions are alternate angles.

questions.subunit: Parallel Lines and Angles
questions.question: A line crosses two parallel lines. When one of a pair of corresponding angles is 72°, what is the measure of the other corresponding angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so it is 72°.

questions.subunit: Parallel Lines and Angles
questions.question: A line crosses two parallel lines. When one of a pair of alternate angles is 55°, what is the measure of the other alternate angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so it is 55°.

questions.subunit: Parallel Lines and Angles
questions.question: A line crosses two parallel lines ℓ and m. When the angle formed on the ℓ side is 120°, what is the measure of the co-interior angle (same-side interior angle) on the m side, in degrees?
questions.explanation: For parallel lines, co-interior angles add up to 180°. 180°-120°=60°.

questions.subunit: Parallel Lines and Angles
questions.question: When a line crosses two lines and the corresponding angles are equal, what can we say about the two lines?
questions.explanation: If corresponding angles (or alternate angles) are equal, the two lines are parallel. This is the condition for lines to be parallel.

questions.subunit: Interior and Exterior Angles of a Triangle
questions.question: When two interior angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°, what is the measure of the remaining interior angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 180°-50°-60°=70°.

questions.subunit: Interior and Exterior Angles of a Triangle
questions.question: When two interior angles of a triangle are 45° and 75°, what is the measure of the exterior angle next to the remaining interior angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles. 45°+75°=120°.

questions.subunit: Interior and Exterior Angles of a Triangle
questions.question: For a triangle, one exterior angle is 130°, and one of its non-adjacent interior angles is 55°. What is the measure of the other non-adjacent interior angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles. 130°-55°=75°.

questions.subunit: Interior and Exterior Angles of a Triangle
questions.question: What do we call a triangle whose three interior angles are all acute (less than 90°)?
questions.explanation: If all angles are acute, it is an acute triangle. If one is a right angle, it is a right triangle; if one is obtuse, it is an obtuse triangle.

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of an n-gon is 180°×(n-2). 180°×3=540°.

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon, in degrees?

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: What is the sum of the exterior angles of a polygon, in degrees (the value is the same for any polygon)?
questions.explanation: The sum of the exterior angles of a polygon is always 360°.

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: What is the measure of one interior angle of a regular hexagon, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The sum of the interior angles is 180°×4=720°. Since a regular hexagon has equal angles, 720°÷6=120°.

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: What is the measure of one exterior angle of a regular dodecagon (12-gon), in degrees?
questions.explanation: The sum of the exterior angles is 360°. Since a regular dodecagon has equal angles, 360°÷12=30°.

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: A regular polygon has one exterior angle of 40°. How many sides does it have? Answer with the number only.
questions.explanation: 360°÷40°=9, so it is a regular nonagon (9-gon).

questions.subunit: Sum of the Interior and Exterior Angles of a Polygon
questions.question: A polygon has interior angles that add up to 1440°. How many sides does it have? Answer with the number only.
questions.explanation: From 180°×(n-2)=1440°, we get n-2=8, so n=10. It is a decagon.

questions.subunit: Congruence Conditions for Triangles
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid congruence condition for triangles?
choices: Three pairs of angles are respectively equal
Three pairs of sides are respectively equal
Two pairs of sides and the included angle are respectively equal
One pair of sides and the angles at both of its ends are respectively equal
questions.answer: Three pairs of angles are respectively equal
questions.explanation: Even if three pairs of angles are equal, the triangles may be similar but different in size, so this is not a congruence condition.

questions.subunit: Congruence Conditions for Triangles
questions.question: In △ABC and △DEF, it is known that AB=DE, BC=EF, and ∠B=∠E. Which congruence condition do you use?
choices: Two pairs of sides and the included angle are respectively equal
Three pairs of sides are respectively equal
One pair of sides and the angles at both of its ends are respectively equal
The hypotenuse and one other side are respectively equal
questions.answer: Two pairs of sides and the included angle are respectively equal
questions.explanation: Since ∠B is the angle between AB and BC, the condition 'two pairs of sides and the included angle' can be used.

questions.subunit: Congruence Conditions for Triangles
questions.question: In △ABC and △DEF, it is known that BC=EF, ∠B=∠E, and ∠C=∠F. Which congruence condition do you use?
choices: One pair of sides and the angles at both of its ends are respectively equal
Two pairs of sides and the included angle are respectively equal
Three pairs of sides are respectively equal
Two pairs of angles are respectively equal
questions.answer: One pair of sides and the angles at both of its ends are respectively equal
questions.explanation: Since ∠B and ∠C are the angles at both ends of side BC, the condition 'one pair of sides and the angles at both of its ends' can be used.

questions.subunit: The Congruence Symbol and Corresponding Parts
questions.question: When △ABC≡△DEF, which angle corresponds to ∠A?
questions.explanation: In the congruence statement, corresponding vertices are written in the same order. A↔D, B↔E, C↔F.

questions.subunit: The Congruence Symbol and Corresponding Parts
questions.question: When △ABC≡△DEF and AB=5cm, which side has a length of 5cm?
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides are equal. AB corresponds to DE (A↔D, B↔E).

questions.subunit: How Proofs Work
questions.question: In the statement 'If AB=CD, then AB+EF=CD+EF', what do we call the 'AB=CD' part?
questions.explanation: The part before 'then' is the hypothesis, and the part after it is the conclusion.

questions.subunit: How Proofs Work
questions.question: In a proof, which of the following is already accepted as true and can be used as a reason?
choices: The statement you are trying to prove
An angle that happened to be equal when measured
questions.explanation: A property already accepted as true (a theorem) can be used as a reason. The statement you are trying to prove itself, measurements, and conjectures cannot be used as reasons.

questions.subunit: How Proofs Work
questions.question: After proving that two triangles are congruent, which is the reason used to conclude that corresponding angles are equal?
choices: In congruent figures, corresponding angles are equal
The interior angles of a triangle add up to 180°
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal
questions.answer: In congruent figures, corresponding angles are equal
questions.explanation: We derive the conclusion using the property of congruent figures (corresponding sides and angles are equal).
